records.storyHeadline: A second time scale, made legible
records.storyLead: Explorer II pairs conventional hour and minute reading with an orange 24-hour hand and a fixed graduated bezel, helping distinguish day from night when the sun is not a reliable guide.
records.storyBody: Rolex lists reference 226570 in Oystersteel with a white dial. Its independently adjustable local hour hand, date and 24-hour display are driven by calibre 3285. This page records Rolex-sourced specifications, not a Venturo product or offer.
records.galleryDescription: A Venturo-made functional diagram explains the fixed 24-hour scale and separate 24-hour hand. It is schematic only and is not product photography or an exact variant image.
records.galleryCaption: Original functional schematic · not a Rolex product image and not a model configuration.
records.featureBody1: The dedicated orange hand completes one turn in 24 hours and points to the fixed bezel graduations, distinguishing a second time scale from the central 12-hour display.
records.featureBody2: Rolex identifies this reference as a white-dial Explorer II. The bezel is fixed and graduated for the orange 24-hour hand; it does not rotate as a diver’s timing bezel.
records.featureBody3: Rolex lists a GMT function, independent rapid-setting of the local hour hand, instantaneous date and approximately 70-hour power reserve for calibre 3285.
records.contextHeading: Built for places without a clear day-night cue
records.contextBody: Rolex dates the Explorer II introduction to 1971 and connects its 24-hour display to expeditions in caves and polar regions. The separately named Explorer II is distinguished by its fixed 24-hour graduated bezel, orange hand and date display.

records.storyHeadline: A second time scale, made legible
records.storyLead: Explorer II pairs conventional hour and minute reading with an orange 24-hour hand and a fixed graduated bezel, helping distinguish day from night when the sun is not a reliable guide.
records.storyBody: Rolex lists reference 226570 in Oystersteel with a black dial. Its independently adjustable local hour hand, date and 24-hour display are driven by calibre 3285. This page records Rolex-sourced specifications, not a Venturo product or offer.
records.galleryDescription: A Venturo-made functional diagram explains the fixed 24-hour scale and separate 24-hour hand. It is schematic only and is not product photography or an exact variant image.
records.galleryCaption: Original functional schematic · not a Rolex product image and not a model configuration.
records.featureBody1: The dedicated orange hand completes one turn in 24 hours and points to the fixed bezel graduations, distinguishing a second time scale from the central 12-hour display.
records.featureBody2: Rolex identifies this reference as a black-dial Explorer II. The bezel is fixed and graduated for the orange 24-hour hand; it does not rotate as a diver’s timing bezel.
records.featureBody3: Rolex lists a GMT function, independent rapid-setting of the local hour hand, instantaneous date and approximately 70-hour power reserve for calibre 3285.
records.contextHeading: Built for places without a clear day-night cue
records.contextBody: Rolex dates the Explorer II introduction to 1971 and connects its 24-hour display to expeditions in caves and polar regions. The separately named Explorer II is distinguished by its fixed 24-hour graduated bezel, orange hand and date display.
